name: Conclusion Indicator Profiling
description: Detects the highly predictable, mathematically forced presence and rigid structure of summative concluding paragraphs.
mechanism: A glaring behavioral hallmark of RLHF-aligned AI writing is the 'compulsory conclusion.' Regardless of the prompt's length, the informal nature of the topic, or the lack of any narrative necessity, commercial LLMs default to neatly summarizing their previously stated points. They execute this using highly predictable, textbook rhetorical markers ('In conclusion', 'Ultimately', 'In summary', 'Overall', 'To sum up'). Conversely, authentic human writing—especially in casual emails, forum posts, or abruptly ending creative and opinion pieces—frequently omits formal summative paragraphs entirely. This method rigorously analyzes the final 15% of a text's structure, mapping explicit summative discourse markers and mathematically comparing the semantic overlap between this concluding section and the main body text. A high semantic redundancy (simply repeating what was just said) paired directly with generic, transitional conclusion markers heavily flags the text as exhibiting an AI's automated, uncreative wrapping behavior.
useCase: Exposing AI-generated essays, emails, blog posts, and articles that artificially and stubbornly append unnecessary, repetitive summaries at the end of the text.
strengths:
• Exhibits an extremely high true-positive detection rate for 'zero-shot' prompts fed to major models like ChatGPT and Claude.
• Captures a high-level, deeply ingrained structural behavioral pattern that naive or rushed prompters rarely think to explicitly disable.
• Very lightweight, computationally cheap, and extraordinarily fast to execute over large batches of documents.
limitations:
• Becomes completely ineffective if the user simply deletes the final paragraph before submission or publication.
• Formal academic essays, scientific papers, and executive summaries naturally require summative conclusions, fundamentally raising the false-positive risk in those rigid domains.
• Applicable only to texts that are long enough (typically >200 words) to trigger the AI's internal 'essay format' generation template.
parameters:
Analysis: Rhetorical End-Structure & Semantic Redundancy
Metric: Summative Marker Frequency vs. Body Semantic Overlap
Output: 0-100 Conclusive Template (Automated Wrap-Up) Score
accuracy: Very High — 85-95% on raw, unmodified AI outputs resulting from generic prompts. Efficacy collapses if the last paragraph is manually pruned.

references.title: Jurafsky, D. & Martin, J.H. (2024). Speech and Language Processing. 3rd Edition.
Guo, B. et al. (2023). How Close is ChatGPT to Human Experts? Comparison Corpus, Evaluation, and Detection. NeurIPS.
